title: Base-change invariance for constant sheaves
statement: Let $k\subseteq k'$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a smooth separated connected curve over $k$, let $\overline C$ be a compactification of $C$ ([lem-sc-compactification]; thus $\overline C=C$ when $C$ is proper), and let $g:=g(\overline C)$ ([def-sc-genus]). Let $n\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. For every $q\geq0$, the pullback map of [def-sc-field-extension] $\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf F_n):H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)\longrightarrow H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\mathbf F_n)$ is an isomorphism; if $C$ is proper it is compatible with the identifications of [lem-sc-pic-proper-ntorsion] and [lem-sc-genus-invariant], and if $C$ is affine with the identifications of [lem-sc-pic-affine].

proof.text: By [lem-sc-base-change-curve], $C_{k'}$ is a smooth separated curve over $k'$ of the same dimension, proper (resp. affine) if $C$ is proper (resp. affine). The algebraically closed field $k$ is separably closed, so the connected scheme $C$ is geometrically connected over $k$ by [lem-weil-separably-closed-geometrically-connected]; by the definition of geometric connectedness [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], applied to the extension $k'/k$, the scheme $C_{k'}$ is connected. Thus $C_{k'}$ is a smooth separated connected curve over the algebraically closed field $k'$, and all the curve statements cited below apply to it as well as to $C$.

Proper case. Let $C$ be proper; by step 1, $C_{k'}$ is a proper smooth connected curve over $k'$, of genus $g$ by [lem-sc-genus-invariant]. By [lem-sc-primitive-root] the trivialization $\theta_\zeta:\mu_n\cong\mathbf F_n$ is compatible with pullback along $k\subseteq k'$, so it suffices to show that pullback is an isomorphism on $H^q(-,\mu_n)$. Both curves have $H^2(-,\mathbf G_m)=0$ by [lem-sc-brauer-zero], so [lem-sc-kummer-les] applies over $k$ and over $k'$, and by [lem-sc-kummer-base-change-compatibility] pullback is a morphism between the two Kummer sequences. For $q=0$: $H^0(-,\mu_n)=\mu_n(k)\to\mu_n(k')$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sc-primitive-root]. For $q=1$: $H^1(C,\mu_n)=\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]$ by [lem-sc-kummer-les], which lies in $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ (the degree takes values in the torsion-free group $\mathbf Z$) and is $(\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z)^{2g}$ by [lem-sc-pic-proper-ntorsion]; under $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)=J_C(k)$ of [thm-sc-jacobian-representability], which is compatible with base change ($J_{C_{k'}}\cong(J_C)_{k'}$) by [lem-sc-genus-invariant], $\rho^1$ becomes the canonical map $J_C[n](k)\to J_C[n](k')$, an isomorphism by [thm-av-final](c). For $q=2$: $H^2(C,\mu_n)=\operatorname{Pic}(C)/n$ by [lem-sc-kummer-les]; since $\operatorname{Pic}^0(C)$ is $n$-divisible ([lem-sc-pic-proper-ntorsion]), the degree identifies it with $\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, generated by the class of a point $P\in C(k)$, which exists by [lem-pc-rational-points-dense]. The pullback of $\mathcal O_C(P)$ is $\mathcal O_{C_{k'}}(P_{k'})$ for the $k'$-rational point $P_{k'}$, again of degree $1$, so the same description over $k'$ shows that $\rho^2$ sends a generator to a generator and is an isomorphism. For $q>2$ both groups vanish by [thm-sc-proper-cohomology]. By construction these isomorphisms are compatible with the identifications of [lem-sc-pic-proper-ntorsion] and [lem-sc-genus-invariant].

Affine case. By [lem-sc-proper-or-affine], $C$ is proper or affine; the proper case is step 2, so let $C$ be affine. By step 1, $C_{k'}$ is a smooth affine connected curve over $k'$. [thm-sc-affine-cohomology], applied over $k$ and over $k'$, gives $H^0=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$, the canonical short exact sequences $0\to\mathcal O(C)^\times/\mathcal O(C)^{\times n}\to H^1(-,\mathbf F_n)\to\operatorname{Pic}(-)[n]\to0$ (obtained from [lem-sc-kummer-les] through $\theta_\zeta$), and $H^q(-,\mathbf F_n)=0$ for $q>1$, so $\rho^q$ is an isomorphism for $q\ge2$. For $q=0$, $\rho^0$ is $\mu_n(k)\to\mu_n(k')$ transported by $\theta_\zeta$, an isomorphism by [lem-sc-primitive-root]. For $q=1$, [lem-sc-kummer-base-change-compatibility] and the compatibility of $\theta_\zeta$ with pullback ([lem-sc-primitive-root]) make pullback a morphism of these short exact sequences; its outer maps are isomorphisms by [lem-sc-units-quotient-base-change] and by the affine clause of [lem-sc-kummer-base-change-compatibility], so $\rho^1$ is an isomorphism by the five lemma, compatibly with the $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]$ of [lem-sc-pic-affine].
